SS.4.CG.1.1.statement_verified: Explain why the Florida government has a written Constitution.

SS.4.CG.1.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize that Florida's constitution protects the rights of Florida's citizens and identifies the parts and functions of state government.

SS.4.CG.2.1.statement_verified: Identify and describe how citizens work with local and state governments to solve problems.

SS.4.CG.2.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize how citizens work with government to solve community problems.

SS.4.CG.2.2.statement_verified: Explain the importance of voting, public service, and volunteerism to the state and nation.

SS.4.CG.2.AP.2.statement_verified: Identify different types of public service and volunteerism.

SS.4.CG.2.3.statement_verified: Identify individuals who represent the citizens of Florida at the state level.

SS.4.CG.2.AP.3.statement_verified: Recognize that Florida has a representative government.

SS.4.CG.3.AP.2.statement_verified: Identify the structures of local and state governments.

SS.4.E.1.1.statement_verified: Identify entrepreneurs from various demographic backgrounds who have influenced Florida and local economy.

SS.4.E.1.AP.2.statement_verified: Identify important economic contributions of Florida.

SS.4.FL.1.1.statement_verified: People have many different types of jobs from which to choose. Identify different jobs requiring people to have different skills.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.1.statement_verified: Identify different skills with different types of jobs.

SS.4.FL.1.2.statement_verified: People earn an income when they are hired by an employer to work at a job. Explain why employers are willing to pay people to do their work.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.2.statement_verified: Recognize that people get paid for their work.

SS.4.FL.1.3.statement_verified: Workers are paid for their labor in different ways such as wages, salaries, or commissions. Explain the ways in which workers are paid.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.3.statement_verified: Recognize that workers are paid in different ways for different jobs.

SS.4.FL.1.4.statement_verified: People can earn interest income from letting other people borrow their money. Explain why banks and financial institutions pay people interest when they deposit their money at those institutions.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.4.statement_verified: Identify interest income from people borrowing money.

SS.4.FL.1.5.statement_verified: People can earn income by renting their property to other people. Identify different types of property (such as apartments, automobiles, or tools) that people own and on which rent is paid.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.5.statement_verified: Recognize income can be earned by renting to others.

SS.4.FL.1.6.statement_verified: Describe ways that people who own a business can earn a profit, which is a source of income.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.6.statement_verified: Recognize that people who own a business can make money.

SS.4.FL.1.7.statement_verified: Entrepreneurs are people who start new businesses. Entrepreneurs do not know if their new businesses will be successful and earn a profit. Identify ways in which starting a business is risky for entrepreneurs.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.7.statement_verified: Recognize that entrepreneurs are people who start new businesses.

SS.4.FL.1.8.statement_verified: Income earned from working and most other sources of income are taxed. Describe ways that the revenue from these taxes is used to pay for government provided goods and services.

SS.4.FL.1.AP.8.statement_verified: Recognize taxes are used to pay for government goods and services.

SS.4.FL.2.1.statement_verified: Explain that economic wants are desires that can be satisfied by consuming a good, a service, or a leisure activity.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.1.statement_verified: Identify economic wants with goods, services, and leisure activities.

SS.4.FL.2.2.statement_verified: Explain that people make choices about what goods and services they buy because they can’t have everything they want. This requires individuals to prioritize their wants.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.2.statement_verified: Place goods and services in a list that prioritizes an individual's wants.

SS.4.FL.2.3.statement_verified: Identify some of the ways that people spend a portion of their income on goods and services in order to increase their personal satisfaction or happiness.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.3.statement_verified: Recognize a portion of income can be used for personal happiness.

SS.4.FL.2.4.statement_verified: Discuss that whenever people buy something, they incur an opportunity cost. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up when a person makes a choice.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.4.statement_verified: Recognize a scenario that involves making an economic choice.

SS.4.FL.2.5.statement_verified: Explain that costs are things that a decision maker gives up; benefits are things that a decision maker gains. Make an informed decision by comparing the costs and benefits of spending alternatives.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.5.statement_verified: Identify the costs and benefits of spending based on an informed decision.

SS.4.FL.2.6.statement_verified: Predict how people’s spending choices are influenced by prices as well as many other factors, including advertising, the spending choices of others, and peer pressure.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.6.statement_verified: Identify ways people's spending choices are influenced.

SS.4.FL.2.7.statement_verified: Planning for spending can help people make informed choices. Develop a budget plan for spending, saving, and managing income.

SS.4.FL.2.AP.7.statement_verified: Identify the parts of a budget plan (spending, saving, and managing income).

SS.4.FL.3.1.statement_verified: Identify ways that income is saved, spent on goods and services, or used to pay taxes.

SS.4.FL.3.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize ways that income is used.

SS.4.FL.3.2.statement_verified: Explain that when people save money, they give up the opportunity to buy things now in order to buy things later.

SS.4.FL.3.AP.2.statement_verified: Recognize that saving money involves choices

SS.4.FL.3.3.statement_verified: Identify ways that people can choose to save money in many places—for example, at home in a piggy bank or at a commercial bank, credit union, or savings and loan.

SS.4.FL.3.AP.3.statement_verified: Identify places where people can save money.

SS.4.FL.3.4.statement_verified: Identify savings goals people set as incentives to save. One savings goal might be to buy goods and services in the future.

SS.4.FL.3.AP.4.statement_verified: Identify the relationship between saving money and future purchases.

SS.4.FL.3.5.statement_verified: Explain that when people deposit money into a bank (or other financial institution), the bank may pay them interest. Banks attract savings by paying interest. People also deposit money into banks because banks are safe places to keep their savings.

SS.4.FL.3.AP.5.statement_verified: Recognize the advantages of saving money in a bank.

SS.4.FL.4.1.statement_verified: Discuss that interest is the price the borrower pays for using someone else’s money.

SS.4.FL.4.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize that interest is added when you borrow money.

SS.4.FL.4.2.statement_verified: Identify instances when people use credit, that they receive something of value now and agree to repay the lender over time, or at some date in the future, with interest.

SS.4.FL.4.AP.2.statement_verified: Identify an instance when people use a loan.

SS.4.FL.5.1.statement_verified: Explain that after people have saved some of their income, they must decide how to invest their savings so that it can grow over time.

SS.4.FL.5.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize the difference between saving and financial investing.

SS.4.FL.5.2.statement_verified: Explain that a financial investment is the purchase of a financial asset, such as a stock, with the expectation of an increase in the value of the asset and/or increase in future income.

SS.4.FL.5.AP.2.statement_verified: Recognize that an investment may or may not produce a future income.

SS.4.FL.6.1.statement_verified: Explain that risk is the chance of loss or harm.

SS.4.FL.6.AP.1.statement_verified: Recognize common examples of a risk.

SS.4.FL.6.2.statement_verified: Explain that risk from accidents and unexpected events is an unavoidable part of daily life.

SS.4.FL.6.AP.2.statement_verified: Recognize that unexpected events are part of daily life.

SS.4.FL.6.3.statement_verified: Describe ways that individuals can either choose to accept risk or take steps to protect themselves by avoiding or reducing risk.

SS.4.FL.6.AP.3.statement_verified: Identify ways to avoid or reduce risks.

SS.4.FL.6.4.statement_verified: Discuss that one method to cope with unexpected losses is to save for emergencies.

SS.4.FL.6.AP.4.statement_verified: Recognize a benefit of emergency savings.
